html:
The Oohenumpa, or Two Kettles, are one of the seven bands of the Lakota, the western Sioux. The map places them in central South Dakota, along the Missouri River.

In 1492 the ancestors of the Lakota still lived further east, around the woodlands and prairies of Minnesota. They moved west onto the Plains in the 1700s, took up the horse (horses reached the Plains from Spanish New Mexico) and built their lives around the bison hunt. The Two Kettles were one of the smaller bands. By the treaties of the 1850s and 1860s they were inside the Great Sioux Reservation, and after the bison slaughter and the breakup of that reservation in 1889 they settled on the Cheyenne River Reservation, which they share with other Lakota bands, near the Cheyenne River.
